title: Boosted regression trees map groundwater pH in the glacial aquifer system
summary: A boosted regression tree model trained on pH from 18,386 wells predicted three-dimensional pH across the glacial aquifer system, with R2 0.60 on held-out data. Carbonate content combined with long flowpaths drives alkaline conditions, and predicted pH above 7.5, linked to arsenic mobilization, is more common than pH below 6 at drinking-water depths. The authors state the model is not meant for precise local estimates; the test split is from the same compiled dataset.
ai_technology: Boosted regression tree including modeled groundwater age and flowpath length as predictors

evidence.tested: Held-out testing wells from the compiled dataset, comparing boosted regression tree variants.
evidence.unknown: Independent-region validation; spatial autocorrelation was not assessed in the excerpt read.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts three-dimensional pH from hydrogeologic predictors
